sources.title: WHO Global Air Quality Guidelines & Disease Burden
sources.extractedText: Ambient air pollution causes an estimated 4.2 million premature deaths worldwide per year. Approximately 99% of the global population breathes air exceeding WHO guideline limits. Water pollution affects millions with over 80% of global wastewater discharged without treatment.

sources.title: UN Water Development Report: Wastewater and Water Quality
sources.publisher: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)
sources.extractedText: Agricultural runoff represents 42% of global freshwater pollution, while industrial discharge accounts for 28% and municipal sewage contributes 18% of global aquatic pollutant loading.

sources.title: EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations
sources.extractedText: EPA sets Maximum Contaminant Levels (MCL) for drinking water contaminants including Lead (0.015 mg/L), Nitrate (10.0 mg/L), Arsenic (0.010 mg/L), and Benzene (0.005 mg/L) to prevent systemic human toxicity.

sources.title: Lancet Commission on Pollution and Health Report
sources.extractedText: Pollution remains responsible for approximately 9.0 million premature deaths per year worldwide, accounting for 1 in 6 deaths globally. Pollution-related disease causes global welfare losses totaling $4.6 trillion annually.

evidence.claim: Ambient air pollution causes an estimated 4.2 million premature deaths worldwide per year.
Approximately 99% of the global population breathes air exceeding WHO guideline limits.
Water pollution affects millions with over 80% of global wastewater discharged without treatment.
Agricultural runoff represents 42% of global freshwater pollution, while industrial discharge accounts for 28% and municipal sewage contributes 18% of global aquatic pollutant loading.

EPA sets Maximum Contaminant Levels (MCL) for drinking water contaminants including Lead (0.015 mg/L), Nitrate (10.0 mg/L), Arsenic (0.010 mg/L), and Benzene (0.005 mg/L) to prevent systemic human toxicity.
Pollution remains responsible for approximately 9.0 million premature deaths per year worldwide, accounting for 1 in 6 deaths globally.
Pollution-related disease causes global welfare losses totaling $4.6 trillion annually.
